name: Prefrontal Cortex (Dorsolateral & Ventromedial)
function: Executive functioning, working memory, cognitive flexibility, abstract reasoning, decision-making, and emotional/impulse regulation.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Apathy, severe impulsivity, perseveration, poor risk assessment, utilization behavior, and personality changes (e.g., Phineas Gage pattern).

name: Broca's Area (Inferior Frontal Gyrus)
function: Motor planning and execution of expressive language, articulation, and complex syntax construction.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Non-fluent, effortful, telegraphic speech with agrammatism; writing is similarly impaired, but auditory comprehension remains relatively intact.

name: Primary Motor Cortex (Precentral Gyrus)
function: Executes contralateral voluntary motor movements via the corticospinal tract, mapped topographically as the motor homunculus.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Weakness or paralysis on the opposite side of the body, spasticity, and hyperreflexia.

name: Primary Somatosensory Cortex (Postcentral Gyrus)
function: Processes tactile sensations including touch, pain, temperature, pressure, and proprioception from the contralateral side of the body.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Inability to perceive touch or recognize objects by feel alone (astereognosis) on the opposite side of the body.

name: Posterior Parietal Cortex & Angular/Supramarginal Gyri
function: Spatial attention, visuospatial integration, sensorimotor transformation, mathematical calculation, and reading processing.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Right lesion leads to left spatial neglect. Dominant (left) BA 39/40 lesion causes Gerstmann Syndrome: acalculia, agraphia, finger agnosia, and left-right disorientation.

name: Wernicke's Area (Superior Temporal Gyrus)
function: Comprehension of spoken and written language, phonological retrieval, and semantic interpretation.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Fluent but empty speech ('word salad'), neologisms, verbal paraphasias, and profound loss of language comprehension.

name: Primary Auditory Cortex (Heschl's Gyrus)
function: Tonotopic processing of sound frequency, pitch, volume, and auditory localization.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Inability to recognize non-verbal environmental sounds or comprehend speech despite functional peripheral auditory pathways.

name: Fusiform Face Area & Inferotemporal Cortex
function: High-level visual object recognition, complex visual category representation, and facial identity recognition.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Inability to recognize familiar faces (prosopagnosia) or identify complex visual objects despite preserved visual acuity.

name: Hippocampus & Medial Temporal Lobe
function: Encoding and consolidation of declarative (explicit) long-term episodic and semantic memories, as well as spatial navigation.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Complete inability to form new episodic long-term memories (e.g., Patient H.M. profile), while procedural memory remains intact.

name: Amygdala
function: Emotional valence assignment, threat detection, fear conditioning, and autonomic stress modulation.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Bilateral damage causes loss of fear responses, hyperorality, hypersexuality, psychic blindness, and emotional blunting.

name: Primary Visual Cortex (Striate Cortex / V1)
function: Retinotopic mapping and processing of visual features like spatial orientation, line contrast, motion, and visual field representation.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Contralateral visual field loss (hemianopia) or complete cortical blindness; sometimes accompanied by Anton-Babinski syndrome (denial of blindness).

name: Arcuate Fasciculus
function: Bidirectional white matter pathway linking Wernicke's and Broca's areas to coordinate language processing and repetition.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Fluent spontaneous speech and intact comprehension, but a severe and isolated inability to repeat spoken words or sentences.

name: Basal Ganglia (Striatum, Globus Pallidus, Subthalamic Nucleus)
function: Action selection, gating of motor movement, habit formation, procedural learning, and reward-based reinforcement.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Hypokinetic disorders (bradykinesia, resting tremor, rigidity) or hyperkinetic movement disorders (chorea, ballism).

name: Thalamus
function: Sensory relay station (relays all sensory modalities except olfaction to cortex) and cortical arousal/consciousness regulation.

clinicalDeficit.condition: Thalamic Pain Syndrome / Korsakoff's Syndrome / Coma
clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Severe sensory loss/pain, confabulation, anterograde memory loss (mammillothalamic damage), or altered consciousness states.

name: Cerebellum
function: Motor coordination, fine precision timing, posture control, motor learning, and cognitive/emotional sequence timing.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Dysmetria (past-pointing), dysdiadochokinesia (inability to perform rapid alternating movements), intention tremor, and wide-based gait.

name: Brainstem (Midbrain, Pons, Medulla Oblongata)
function: Autonomic life-support functions (respiration, cardiovascular control), sleep-wake cycles, cranial nerve functions, and ascending arousal.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Pontine damage causes total paralysis with preserved consciousness (Locked-in); medullary damage is life-threatening due to respiratory arrest.
